{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent cemiplimab dose between synopsis and body",
      "quote": "Cemiplimab 437 mg given by intravenous (IV) infusion over 30 minutes Q3W",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The synopsis states cemiplimab dose as 437 mg, but the body (Section 6.1) states 350 mg. This is a critical discrepancy that must be resolved.",
      "fix": "Align the cemiplimab dose across all sections; verify the correct dose and update accordingly."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent response assessment timepoint",
      "quote": "Patients will be assessed for response at cycle 1 day 52 (week 7)",
      "page": 19,
      "section": "Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis says response assessment at cycle 1 day 52, but the body (Section 6.1) says day 50. This inconsistency could affect visit scheduling and data collection.",
      "fix": "Standardize the response assessment timepoint to either day 50 or day 52 across the protocol."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent CR discontinuation timepoint",
      "quote": "Patients with confirmed complete response (CR) after a minimum of 60 weeks of treatment may elect to discontinue treatment",
      "page": 19,
      "section": "Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis states 60 weeks, but the body (Section 6.1) states 48 weeks. This discrepancy affects patient eligibility for early discontinuation.",
      "fix": "Reconcile the minimum treatment duration for CR discontinuation between synopsis and body."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent sample size between synopsis and statistical plan",
      "quote": "Approximately 126 patients are planned to be enrolled in the study.",
      "page": 19,
      "section": "Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The synopsis states 126 patients, but the Statistical Plan section states 105 patients. This is a critical discrepancy that affects sample size and power calculations.",
      "fix": "Determine the correct sample size and update all sections consistently."
    },
    {
      "title": "Incomplete secondary endpoint list in body",
      "quote": "The secondary endpoints are: adverse events (SAEs) and ≥ grade 3 laboratory abnormalities during the treatment period and up to 90 days after the last dose of study treatment",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "4.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The secondary endpoints section in the body appears truncated; it lists only a fragment of the first endpoint and omits DOR, PFS, and OS that are listed in the synopsis.",
      "fix": "Complete the secondary endpoints list to include all endpoints (TEAEs/AESIs/SAEs, DOR, PFS, OS)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing definition of end of study in body",
      "quote": "The end of the study is defined as the date of the last contact of the last patient in the study.",
      "page": 19,
      "section": "Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The end of study definition is only in the synopsis; the body lacks a dedicated section for 'End of Trial' (M11 4.4), which is required for regulatory clarity.",
      "fix": "Add an 'End of Trial' section in the body with the definition and any relevant procedures."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing contraception and lifestyle restrictions",
      "quote": "pregnancy test for women of childbearing potential",
      "page": 20,
      "section": "Procedures and Assessments",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol mentions pregnancy tests but lacks a dedicated section on contraception requirements and lifestyle restrictions (M11 5.4, 5.5), which are essential for a study with an investigational vaccine and immunotherapy.",
      "fix": "Add sections detailing contraception requirements for males and females, and any lifestyle restrictions (e.g., alcohol, sexual activity)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent cycle 1 day 50 vs day 52 in synopsis",
      "quote": "Patients will be assessed for response at cycle 1 day 52 (week 7)",
      "page": 19,
      "section": "Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "This is a duplicate finding of the day 52 vs 50 discrepancy, but it is important to highlight as it appears in the synopsis and may be overlooked.",
      "fix": "Correct the synopsis to match the body's day 50 or vice versa."
    }
  ]
}
